gen-gf-gabarito-gf-hahmlet: Hahmlet reads like a classic serif with a worn-charcoal softness, its shapes kept widely parted. And Gabarito above it draws every line like a rolling-ball pen, so the page moves from one steady trail to gentle pressure.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-im-fell-english-sc: IM Fell English SC reads bookish and easy, a text serif with moderate contrast and open throats. Gabarito drawn small would lose its flowing curves, though, so give that heading some room to spread.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-inria-serif: Gabarito's strokes hold a tube-like thickness through every bend. Inria Serif underneath has slightly lighter diagonals and wide-mouthed rounds, so the page moves from bold plumbing to quieter, finer lines.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-joan: Joan reads like a text serif with light but visible stroke variation, and the inside of its c is easy to see. Gabarito's single-pen-tip headings sit above it nicely.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-junge: Gabarito draws its heading with a ruler-straight line weight, expressive and distinctive from the first word. Junge answers with medium contrast and no sharp hairlines.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-libertinus-serif: Libertinus Serif reads refined, with a slight swell on its bowls. Gabarito's constant-weight lines trace each heading letter, so the two feel cleanly divided between loud and quiet.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-libre-caslon-text: Expressive is Gabarito's mood, with neon-tube letters of constant thickness bent into every heading. And Libre Caslon Text follows with robust downstrokes and slender turns, so a long page stays comfortable to read.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-lustria: Traditional and authoritative, Lustria lets its stroke weight ebb and flow without drama. But Gabarito's laser-cut heading uses one cutting width, so the two sit together like a sharp sign over a bound volume.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-maitree: Gabarito opens the pair with the sense of one constant pen width, expressive and distinctive. Maitree's quiet contrast makes a classic serif that feels dignified over many lines.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-marcellus: Refined and literary, Marcellus carries a subtle weight change like etched lines in glass. Gabarito's headings hold rounds and stems in one weight, so a long page moves from bold shapes to a steady lettering-pen rhythm.
